我本来在PUBG里只想当个安静的人机质检员。原则很简单：不主动开枪，不抢队友空投，毒圈来了先找车，车炸了先找厕所。结果上周电竞社招新，社长非要看我账号，说“随便看看战绩”。我手一抖，把最近十场记录投到了教室大屏上——十场零杀，场均伤害18，最高排名第二，系统称号“苟活专家”。全班沉默两秒，后排有人喊：“姐，你这运营太稳了吧？”我还没解释那是我边吃泡面边玩的，社长已经拍桌子：“明天校际四排赛，你来当指挥。”我说我连枪都压不住，他说：“要的就是你这种不吃资源还能进决赛圈的。”更离谱的是第二天，学校论坛冒出一个热帖：《电竞社新指挥场均伤害18，疑似隐藏战术大师》。底下有人回“18伤害怎么了，人家用脑子打游戏”，还有人问“学姐收徒吗，我枪法好，听指挥”。从那天起，我课桌里开始出现能量饮料和止痛药，都是男生塞的，说“指挥要保重身体”。我去食堂打饭，选修课坐我后排的两个男生端着餐盘坐我对面，问我：“你平时跳P城还是G港，我跟你。”我说我一般跳野区厕所，他眼睛一亮：“果然是细节控。”晚上更夸张，我一上线，邀请列表跟食堂排队一样。我随便进了一个队，里面三个男生，一个说“我负责架枪”，一个说“我负责开车”，还有一个说“我负责给你报点”。我说：“你们这么强为什么还要我？”他们异口同声：“缺个会苟的。”那天决赛圈，我全程趴在草丛里，连开镜都不敢，结果他们三个把对面灭了，最后一只鸡稳稳落我头上。其中一个男生还发语音：“指挥，这波圈刷得怎么样？”我说：“挺好，就是草有点扎脸。”他们笑成一片。后来事情彻底跑偏。有人把我“0杀吃鸡”的记录印成了传单，贴在宿舍楼下，标题是《想学运营吗？本周四晚，跟18伤害学姐学进圈》。我路过的时候，旁边两个男生小声说：“就是她，听说她连平底锅都不捡，因为怕影响走位。”我想解释，其中一个已经掏出手机：“学姐，能加个好友吗？我保证不给你丢空投。”现在我最怕的不是决赛圈一打四，也不是队友倒地喊救命，而是每天打开游戏，面对一堆“你指挥就行，枪我们来开”的邀请。
那一刻我终于明白，PUBG里最难压的不是枪，是全校想跟我一起跳厕所的热情。

[h1]⚠️ PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS – NOT RECOMMENDED[/h1]

[hr]

[h2]Too Many Cheaters. Not Enough Action.[/h2]

Honestly, PUBG is becoming increasingly frustrating to play because of the ridiculous number of cheaters.

[b]Aimbots, wallhacks, suspicious players and blatant cheating[/b] are ruining match after match. You spend time looting, positioning yourself, and playing strategically, only to get killed by someone who seems to know exactly where you are or never misses a shot.

What's the point of playing a competitive battle royale when legitimate players are constantly punished for playing fair?

[hr]

[h2]What Needs to Change:[/h2]

[list]
[*]Better anti-cheat protection.
[*]Permanent bans for confirmed cheaters.
[*]Faster action against reported players.
[*]More protection for legitimate players.
[*]Less focus on cosmetics and more focus on fixing the game.
[/list]

[hr]

[h2]Final Verdict[/h2]

PUBG has the potential to be an amazing game, but the cheating problem makes it difficult to enjoy.

I'm tired of wasting time in matches ruined by cheaters. Players deserve a fair competitive experience.

[b][color=#ff3333]NOT RECOMMENDED.[/color][/b]

Honestly, PUBG is one of those games that can make you feel like a genius one match and completely useless the next.

The best thing about it is the tension. Dropping into a map, searching for weapons, hearing footsteps nearby and wondering whether someone is camping around the next corner never really gets old. Winning a chicken dinner feels genuinely satisfying because you actually have to work for it.

The gunplay is probably my favourite part. Weapons feel different, recoil takes practice, and you can't just run around shooting everything like it's Call of Duty. Sometimes you need to slow down, listen carefully and think before making a move. Playing with friends makes it even better, especially when everything goes wrong and somehow you still manage to survive.

Of course, PUBG can be seriously frustrating. You can spend 20 minutes looting just to get eliminated by someone you never even saw. The learning curve is pretty rough for new players, and experienced players can make you feel like you have absolutely no idea what you're doing.

The graphics are decent, but the game isn't exactly a visual masterpiece. Performance can also be inconsistent depending on the map, settings and what's happening around you. And yeah, cheaters, suspicious players and occasional technical issues can ruin an otherwise good match.

There's no story to keep you playing. The whole point is getting better, learning the maps, improving your aim and trying to survive longer than everyone else. If you enjoy that competitive loop, you can easily sink hundreds of hours into it without noticing.

Overall, PUBG isn't for everyone. If you prefer fast action with constant shooting, the slower pace and getting sent back to the lobby might annoy you. But if you enjoy tactical gunfights where every decision matters, it's still a very satisfying battle royale.

**8/10 — frustrating as hell sometimes, but that feeling when you finally get the chicken dinner makes you want to queue up for another match.
